item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q003_actin_like_atpase_divergence","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, the catalytic domains of Actin/HSP70, hexokinase, and glycerol kinase are not placed in the same family; they are three separate families within the same superfamily. SCOPe places Actin/HSP70 at c.55.1.1, Hexokinase at c.55.1.3, and Glycerol kinase at c.55.1.4, all under the Actin-like ATPase domain superfamily c.55.1. That superfamily sits in the Ribonuclease H-like motif fold c.55 in the Alpha and beta proteins (a/b) class c. The superfamily assignment is the remote-homology statement: their catalytic domains are inferred to share common ancestry even though the modern proteins use that core in different cellular contexts. It supports transfer of only broad structural and mechanistic expectations for the actin-like ATPase catalytic core, such as a homologous ATP/nucleotide-binding architecture, and it can justify using carefully chosen same-superfamily structures as remote templates for that core. It does not justify transferring family-level substrate specificity, full protein function, regulatory behavior, quaternary state, domain boundaries outside the catalytic domain, or naming one family as a representative of another; fold-level similarity to other c.55 superfamilies is weaker still and should not by itself be treated as evidence of homology.","evidence_used":["list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.55/children?limit=100","list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.55.1/children?limit=100","get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.55","get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.55/parents"]}]}
